The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped arriving
Why, in plain words: A planned renaming of the shop's network ports to a platform-wide naming rule also renamed the port the monitoring system collects the shop's measurements from, and the monitoring setup, which finds that port by its name, was not changed to match, so it had nothing to collect.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 8m 36s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose - not taken
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #535 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped arriving
Incident: MetricsAbsent on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:35 UTC, metrics missing from then
Status: Draft. 0 of 5 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 02:58:52 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:40:58 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 02:43:36 UTC - PR #535, opened as a draft

Summary
No metrics were collected from 02:35 UTC on, and they had not resumed by 02:43:36 UTC, 8 minutes 36 seconds later. The service's own logs reach into that stretch until 02:40 UTC, and they were read up to 02:40:55 UTC. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A planned renaming of the shop's network ports to a platform-wide naming rule also renamed the port the monitoring system collects the shop's measurements from, and the monitoring setup, which finds that port by its name, was not changed to match, so it had nothing to collect. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #535, for a person to review and merge. It was written against main, which does not contain the revision that ran: merged, it changes what runs only once a deploy carries it. Until a deploy carries a matching scrape port name, io-shop's metrics stay uncollected, and any real fault in the shop could go unseen by alerts that work from those metrics.

Impact
at least 8m 36s - since onset, metrics missing
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none so far - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: No metrics received from io-shop since 2026-11-11T02:35:00Z - 5m with no sample, against a scrape interval of 15 seconds. The series stopped rather than crossing a threshold, so nothing here says whether the shop is well: these minutes have no readings to judge, not readings that look bad.
The metrics stop at the onset, so the duration is how long they had been missing by the close - not a stretch the service is known to have spent broken.
The service's own logs reach into the stretch the metrics missed until 02:40 UTC: G46bc, Gbac1. They were read up to 02:40:55 UTC, when the alert was raised. As far as they show, the service went on serving as it had before the metrics stopped.

Root cause and contributing factors
The deployment renamed the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml, but deploy/scrape.yaml at that revision still picks the endpoint to scrape by the name `metrics`. The ServiceMonitor selects by port name, and a name that matches no port does not raise an error to the operator. It just gives an empty target list, so Prometheus had nothing to scrape.
Causal chain
symptom Nobody using the shop was seen to have anything go wrong. What was seen instead: the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and the series went absent rather than crossing a threshold.
  Evidence:
    AL1
    T4 02:41:19 Investigator Agent: Read the service's metrics - they stop after the minute at 02:34, and nothing covers the minutes since
    G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 42 occurrences in 29 minutes, 02:06–02:34. After they stopped: 11 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:35–02:40
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 25 occurrences in 29 minutes, 02:06–02:34; # was 0.50% to 4.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 02:24. After they stopped: 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:35–02:40; # was 0.50% to 2.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 02:39
why 1 The metrics stopped because Prometheus had no target to scrape. At the revision that was running, the ServiceMonitor picks the endpoint by the port name `metrics` (S1), and no port at that revision has that name: the metrics port is named `http-metrics` (S2). The scrape config itself says that a name matching no port gives an empty target list, not an error.
  Evidence:
    S1 deploy/scrape.yaml at c3c36da
    S2 deploy/values-production.yaml at c3c36da
why 2 No port was named `metrics` any more because the deploy of revision c3c36da at 02:35:15 UTC renamed every port to the `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, including the metrics port, from `metrics` to `http-metrics` (D1). As of 02:41:33 UTC, all replicas were running that revision.
  Evidence:
    P2 02:35:15 UTC deploy c3c36da by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision c3c36da to io-shop, compared against 2c8f731 - the revision deployed before it.
    T12 02:41:33 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision c3c36da, deployed at 02:35:15
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f731: metrics were still collected with it in place, up to the minute before the onset.
      P1 Nov 10, 2026, 22:35:15 UTC deploy 2c8f731 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
      T4
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:41:34.
      T15
why 3 The rename broke scraping because the change edited only deploy/values-production.yaml and left the scrape config still selecting the port by its old name.
  Evidence:
    D1
    S1
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that the port name the ServiceMonitor selects agrees with the metrics port name in values-production.yaml. The scrape config at the revision that ran says that nothing checks this, so a change to only one of the two files could ship. (AI-2)
- When the ServiceMonitor selects a port name that matches no port, the operator does not raise an error; it gives an empty target list. No alert on an empty scrape target list was seen, so the gap was found only by the MetricsAbsent rule once samples had been missing for its window. (AI-3)
- The MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-4)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The deployment at 02:35:15 UTC renamed every port to the estate-wide <protocol>[-<purpose>] convention. This included the metrics port, which went from metrics to http-metrics. The scrape still selects the old name, so the metrics stopped at 02:35 UTC. The shop itself kept serving at its usual error level. | 0.82 | never tried: the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose
C2 | The deployment changed a configuration value (the metrics port name) and broke scraping. This is the same change, read as an unintended breakage instead of a deliberate convention. | 0.12 | never tried: the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose

Trigger
Suspected, not confirmed: deploy/values-production.yaml went from metrics to http-metrics at 02:35:15 UTC, in the deploy of c3c36da that kuki started.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | 02:41:39 | Refused to act on C1 - the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken
 | 02:43:36 | Proposed a fix: PR #535 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The metrics on io-shop stopped at 02:35 UTC. MetricsAbsent fired at 02:40:55 UTC, 5 minutes 55 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #535 | open
AI-2 | Make the check that the ServiceMonitor's endpoint port name matches the metrics port name in values-production.yaml a required CI gate on every change to deploy/, so a rename that updates only one file is blocked. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Add an alert that fires when the io-shop ServiceMonitor resolves to no scrape targets. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Route the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop to the on-call rotation so it pages a person. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Once the scrape port fix is merged, deploy a revision that carries it to io-shop. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- 38 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision c3c36da, deployed at 02:35:15.
- 39 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:41:34.
- 44 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus refused to act on C1 - the only action that would test the candidate undoes a change that was made on purpose.
- 2 minutes 41 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #535.
What went wrong
- The alert came 3 minutes 25 seconds later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the metrics' stopping is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

After they stopped: 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:35–02:40; # was 0.50% to 2.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 02:39
What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision c3c36da to io-shop, compared against 2c8f731 - the revision deployed before it.
modified deploy/values-production.yaml
  @@ -31,16 +31,19 @@ autoscaling:
     scaleDownStabilizationSeconds: 0
   
   # The ports the shop serves on, each selected by name rather than number.
  +#
  +# Every port is named for the protocol it carries, then what it is for:
  +# `<protocol>[-<purpose>]`. The platform's convention, applied estate-wide.
   ports:
     web:
       port: 8000
  -    portName: web
  +    portName: http
     admin:
       port: 8081
  -    portName: admin
  +    portName: http-admin

       port: 9090

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault, as main holds it: deploy/values-production.yaml names the metrics port http-metrics (metrics.portName: http-metrics), but deploy/scrape.yaml, the ServiceMonitor, still picks its endpoint with port: metrics. The comment in scrape.yaml says the ServiceMonitor finds the endpoint by the port's name, and that a name matching no port gives "a target list with nothing in it" rather than an error. So with these two files as they are, Prometheus has nothing to scrape. That fits the metrics stopping while the shop kept serving.

About the deployed revision: c3c36da is not in main's history, and I haven't read it. The investigation describes its change as ports.metrics.portName, which is a different key path from main's metrics.portName. All I can say about c3c36da is what the investigation reports: it renamed the metrics port to http-metrics and the scrape still asks for metrics. Everything else here describes main.

The fix: in deploy/scrape.yaml, change the endpoint's port: metrics to port: http-metrics so it matches the name in values-production.yaml. That makes the renamed port safe to keep, so it doesn't need rolling back. Nothing under src/ reads the port name; the comment in values-production.yaml says so too.

The test: the scrape.yaml comment says "Nothing checks that the two agree", so I added tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py as that check. It reads portName from the metrics: block of values-production.yaml and every port: entry under the ServiceMonitor's endpoints:, then asserts they match. It uses plain line reading, because I found no YAML library imported anywhere in the repository. Against main as it stands, it should fail, comparing metrics with http-metrics. With this change it should pass, and it should catch the next rename that only updates one of the two files. Nothing has run it yet.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired
S1 | deploy/scrape.yaml at c3c36da
S2 | deploy/values-production.yaml at c3c36da

○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: Shoppers on io-shop saw nothing wrong, but the measurements the business uses to watch the shop stopped arriving. A planned change renamed the shop's network ports to follow a naming rule used across the platform. That change also renamed the port the monitoring system collects the shop's measurements from. The monitoring setup finds that port by its name and wasn't updated to match, so it had nothing to collect. The problem has lasted {duration}, and Argus estimates its cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. No one was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus chose not to test the suspected cause, because the only way to test it would undo a renaming that was made on purpose. Instead it proposed a fix, which is open as a draft. That fix hasn't been applied yet, so the shop's measurements aren't being collected.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
